correctness_confidence.basis: Analytic reductions are sound, exact d=4 and d=3 simplex results reproduced, and the full degree-600 integer certificate passes.

rigor.basis: Finite exact arithmetic is completed by a proved uniform tail. The d=3 global and local optimality claims are explicitly numerical/conditional.

novelty.basis: New low-dimensional optimisation results are plausible; the Jacobi estimate is correctly acknowledged as weaker than known literature.

significance.basis: Closes one low-dimensional all-degree design case and supplies an improved certified construction in another, with modest mathematical scope.

reproducibility.basis: Full claimed exact certificate was replayed; independently coded binomial evaluation confirms all essential simplex values and active-degree frame values.

summary: Theorems A and B are supported. The dimension-four optimum and uniqueness reduce to a rigid outcome count and a short exact spectrum calculation; the dimension-three rational lower bound is reproduced by the complete integer certificate. No material objection remains in the proved claims. The proposed exact value of Gamma_3 remains an explicitly unproved numerical conjecture.
strengths: Correct use of outcome-simple ceiling excludes every higher outcome count.
The Naimark/Bloch description makes the five-outcome d=3 family compact while enforcing overlaps <=4/9, so the attainment argument has no lost collision boundary.
Known stronger Jacobi inequality is properly acknowledged; the weaker integral bound is sufficient for both rigorous tails.
Positive multipliers plus full quotient gradient rank are stated as a conditional strict-local-maximum criterion, rather than treating finite precision as certification.
weaknesses: The principal d=4 argument is mathematically modest once the inherited spectral formula is granted.
Global d=3 optimality, exact root isolation and the numerical search census were not independently certified; the paper mostly labels these limits accurately.
Historical review and model-serving assertions should remain clearly author-supplied descriptions rather than independent evidence.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact Gamma_4=22018975/7340032 and uniqueness of the regular five-outcome simplex, minimum at harmonic degree six.
Exact feasible five-outcome d=3 construction proving Gamma_3>=1.776009937964733 and excluding both ONB and simplex as global optimisers.
